body.statement: Can one add no new model assumption but nevertheless obtain an existing subsequential limit of \(\mathcal I_m(\beta;S_m,Z_{S_m})\), establish triangular-array LAN relative to that limit, localize arbitrary measurable normalized actions, and transfer the Gaussian quadratic loss with curvature \(\Gamma(\beta)\) to the exact Horvitz--Thompson action regret?  The handle is a subsequence audit of the empirical score-information measures followed by a conditional Gaussian-shift decision argument and the finite-boundary comparison.
body.justification: This question separates the missing information limit from the missing exact-action comparison.
body.gap: Armstrong's LAN efficiency results require an information limit and do not provide the exact Horvitz--Thompson boundary transfer.
body.consumer: Resolving it would determine whether the candidate trace constant is an attainable and minimax action-regret coefficient.

obligation.what_is_open: A subsequential empirical score-information limit, triangular-array LAN, arbitrary-action localization, and exact Horvitz--Thompson curvature transfer.
obligation.obstruction: Weak convergence of baseline empirical measures controls bounded continuous functions, but the current assumptions impose no baseline continuity on conditional score second moments; the exact finite-boundary comparison is also unresolved.
obligation.attempted: Factored the pilot likelihood and computed its conditional information. A rational-grid finite-support family shows directly that the random empirical information can converge to a matrix different from the defined population information.
obligation.partial_result: The exact likelihood factorization and conditional information identity are proved.  An explicit rational-grid finite-support family shows that \(\mathcal I_m(\beta;S_m,Z_{S_m})\) need not converge to \(I(\beta)\); a LAN-to-action conclusion therefore requires a subsequential information analysis and the still-open finite-boundary bridge.
